title: Home networking basics: modem, router and the Wi-Fi password

videos.script: Almost everybody has one box in the hall with lights on it, and almost nobody knows which half of it is doing what. {{box}} That matters more than it sounds. Two different machines live in that box — one that talks to the street, and one that talks to your house — and when the internet stops working, which of them failed decides everything you do next. {{two}} This lesson is the home network as a thing with parts. Where the addresses come from and why every house on the road uses the same ones. What the two radios are for, and why the faster one reaches fewer rooms. {{radio}} Then the two passwords — the one you give visitors, and the one almost nobody has ever changed, which is the one that matters. {{pass}} And finally, when it is slow or dead, the four places the problem can be, and the two minutes that tell you which. That part is a rehearsal for the next lesson, where the same method is applied to a computer rather than a network.
